intro: Counting is where all math begins. This branch builds counting from 1 to 120, recognizing small amounts at a glance, and counting in steps of 2, 5 and 10.

I.1.01.what: Counting a group of things by pointing to each one once and saying one number for each.

levels.a: Counts up to 3 things, touching each one.
levels.c: Counts up to 10 things in a line.
levels.d: Counts up to 10 things scattered around, without skipping or counting any twice.

I.1.02.what: Knowing the counting words (one, two, three…) and saying them in the right order.

levels.a: Says the number words from one to three in order.
levels.b: Says the number words up to five and knows which comes next.
levels.c: Says the number words up to ten and knows which comes next.
levels.d: Starts counting from any number, such as seven, and carries on.

I.1.03.what: Counting past ten up to twenty, and noticing that the teen numbers are ten plus a few more.

levels.a: Fills in missing numbers when counting from 10 to 15.
levels.b: Fills in missing numbers when counting from 15 to 20.
levels.c: Sees that a teen number like 12 is ten and 2 more.
levels.d: Counts up to 20 objects, using a full row of ten as a head start.

I.1.04.what: Counting up to fifty, including the tricky moment when one group of ten ends and the next begins.

levels.a: Knows the names of the tens: ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty.
levels.b: Fills in missing numbers when counting within one group of ten, like 14 to 17.
levels.c: Counts across into the next ten, such as 19 to 20 or 29 to 30.
levels.d: Fills in missing numbers anywhere from 1 to 50.

I.1.05.what: Counting from fifty all the way up to one hundred twenty, including going past one hundred.

levels.a: Fills in missing numbers when counting from 50 to 100.
levels.c: Reads and counts numbers from 100 to 120, such as one hundred sixteen.
levels.d: Continues counting from any number up to 120.

I.1.06.what: Recognizing written numbers (numerals) from 0 to 20 and matching them to their names and amounts.

levels.a: Reads the numbers 0 to 10 and matches each to its word.
levels.b: Reads the numbers 11 to 20, such as finding 12 for twelve.
levels.c: Picks out a number that is written the right way round, not flipped.
levels.d: Matches a written number to a picture showing that many.

I.1.07.what: Understanding that the last number said when counting tells how many there are altogether.

levels.a: Knows the last number counted tells how many in all.
levels.b: Answers how many from someone else's count, without counting again.
levels.c: Counts out an exact amount, such as finding the box with exactly 4.
levels.d: Knows the total stays the same whichever end you start counting from.

I.1.08.what: Understanding zero as the number for nothing at all.

levels.a: Knows zero means none, such as an empty plate.
levels.b: Picks out the picture that shows zero things.
levels.c: Writes 0 when there is nothing to count.
levels.d: Knows that 0 comes after 1 when counting backward.

I.1.09.what: Seeing how many are in a small group, up to five, at a quick glance without counting one by one.

levels.a: Says how many at a glance for 1 to 3 dots.
levels.b: Says how many at a glance for 4 or 5 dots.
levels.c: Recognizes the dot patterns on dice.
levels.d: Recognizes how many fingers are held up without counting.

I.1.10.what: Seeing amounts up to ten at a glance, often by spotting a group of five and some more.

levels.a: Says how many counters are in a row of five boxes (a five-frame).
levels.b: Says how many counters are in two rows of five boxes (a ten-frame).
levels.c: Sees two groups, like 5 and 1, and knows the total quickly.
levels.d: Says how many dots at a glance, however they are arranged.

I.1.11.what: Adding a few more by starting from a number and counting up from there, instead of counting everything.

levels.a: Starts at a number and counts on 1 more, staying within 10.
levels.b: Starts at a number and counts on 2 more, staying within 10.
levels.c: Starts from a given number and counts on the extra dots shown.
levels.d: Chooses to start from the bigger number, which makes counting on quicker.
levels.e: Works backwards: finds how many were counted on, or which number it started from.
levels.f: Follows a pattern of jumps by 2 and decides which number it will land on.

I.1.12.what: Counting backward, one number at a time, which later helps with taking away.

levels.a: Counts back from 5, such as jumping back along a number line.
levels.d: Counts back past 10 into single digits, such as 14 down to 9.

I.1.13.what: Knowing what number is just one more or one less than a given number.

levels.a: Finds one more than a number up to 10.
levels.b: Finds one less than a number up to 10.
levels.c: Finds one more or one less for numbers up to 20.
levels.d: The same with numbers up to 100.
levels.e: Follows a chain of steps, like 2 more then 1 less, to find where it ends.
levels.f: Solves a puzzle: two neighbouring numbers add up to a total; finds one of them.

I.1.14.what: Counting in jumps of ten: 10, 20, 30, and so on.

levels.c: Counts by tens from any number, such as 8, 18, 28, 38.
levels.d: Counts bars of ten cubes by tens to find the total.
levels.e: Works backwards, counting down by tens to fill in missing numbers.
levels.f: Works out how many numbers are said when counting by tens, such as from 8 to 88.

I.1.15.what: Counting in jumps of five: 5, 10, 15, 20, and so on.

levels.d: Counts hands of five fingers, or 5-cent coins, by fives.

I.1.16.what: Counting in jumps of two: 2, 4, 6, 8, and so on.

levels.c: Counts objects in pairs to find how many.
levels.d: Counts by twos starting from any even number, such as 30.
levels.e: Spots the one wrong number in a count by twos.
levels.f: Counts how many even numbers lie between two numbers, such as 13 and 27.
